previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with asymptomatic hypotension (70/50) noted at dialysis and increased right hip and knee pain. He has a history of ESRD, recent MRSA line infection on vancomycin, non-ischemic cardiomyopathy, and prior CVA with residual right leg weakness. Initial workup revealed hyperkalemia, treated emergently, and a new left femoral central line was placed for dialysis access. Imaging showed avascular necrosis of the right femoral head with joint degeneration and an old acetabular fracture. Knee aspiration was performed after initial refusal, with no growth on culture, ruling out septic arthritis. Blood cultures remained negative. He was managed conservatively with continuation of vancomycin for the prior MRSA infection, adjustment of dialysis fluid removal, and initiation of midodrine to support blood pressure during dialysis. Orthopedics recommended outpatient follow-up for possible hip replacement. The patient was discharged home with services, stable and afebrile, with clear instructions on medication, weight monitoring, and follow-up.

radiology_notes.text:
RIGHT HIP ASPIRATION UNDER FLUOROSCOPIC GUIDANCE

CLINICAL HISTORY:  Hip pain.  Assess for infection.

COMPARISON:  MRI ___.

PROCEDURE:  Fluoroscopic-guided right hip aspiration.

TECHNIQUE:  The patient was informed of possible benefits, risks and
alternatives.  Written consent was obtained.  A pre-procedural timeout was
performed using at least 3 patient identifiers including name, birthday, and
medical record number.  Site and side of the procedure, as well as procedure
to be performed were confirmed by the patient.  

An appropriate spot was marked and the area was prepped and draped in a
standard sterile fashion.  Local anesthesia in the form of 1% lidocaine was
injected into the skin and subcutaneous soft tissues.  Under direct
fluoroscopic guidance, an 18-gauge spinal needle was advanced into the right
hip joint.  Successful positioning was confirmed by the instillation of a
small amount of Optiray contrast material.  A syringe was attached to the
needle, and a total of 0.5 mL of serosanguinous joint fluid was aspirated
after multiple attempts in three different locations within the joint.  A
small amount of optiray contrast material was then injected to confirm needle
position.  The sample was sent to the lab in three separate containers for
gram stain and culture from the three different areas.  There was not enough
sample to send for cell count and differential.

The needle was removed, hemostasis was achieved, and a sterile dry bandage was
placed.

The patient tolerated the procedure well without complications.

FINDINGS:
1.  Radiopaque contrast is present in the right hip joint space.
2.  Severe flattening and sclerosis of the femoral head with joint space
narrowing and protrusio acetabulum, similar to the previous MRI.  There is
prominent heterotopic ossification adjacent to the acetabulum.

IMPRESSION:
1.  Status post right hip aspiration.
2.  Findings are consistent with avascular necrosis and secondary degenerative
change.

Dr. ___ was present and provided direct supervision during the procedure.

HISTORY:  Possible insufficiency fracture of the left hip.

FINDINGS:  In comparison with the study of ___, there is little overall
change.  Probable old fracture of the right acetabulum with marked muscle
wasting suggesting paraplegia.  Apparent fusion of the sacroiliac joints that
could represent spondyloarthropathy or relate to paraplegia.  Probable AVM of
the right femoral head.

There is severe degenerative change about the left hip with narrowing,
spurring, and subchondral cyst formation.  No definite fracture is
appreciated.  If there is clinical concern for an occult fracture, MRI could
be considered.
